content.text:
What kind of story is The Little Prince?

The Little Prince is a beloved classic in which a little prince from a tiny planet meets a pilot in the desert and shares stories of many planets and the people he has met. It has been cherished for generations for its warm message: "What is most important is invisible to the eyes."

content.alt: The Little Prince - The original story of The Little Prince
content.text:
The original story of The Little Prince

Published in 1943 by French author Saint-Exupery, it is one of the most widely read books in the world. Its heart lies in symbolic characters such as the little prince, the rose, the fox, and the pilot in the desert, and in the idea of "taming."

content.alt: The Little Prince - The Little Prince plot summary
content.text:
The Little Prince plot summary

A pilot who has crash-landed in the desert meets a little prince from a tiny planet. The prince tells him about his own planet and precious rose, the grown-ups he met on various planets, and his friendship with the fox. The realization that "one sees clearly only with the heart" leaves a quiet, moving impression.

content.alt: The Little Prince - The lessons of The Little Prince
content.text:
The lessons of The Little Prince

The core message is that what is most important is invisible to the eyes, and can only be seen clearly with the heart. To nurture the heart that cares for precious relationships, try asking your child, "What is precious to me?"

content.alt: The Little Prince - How to read it aloud to your child
content.text:
How to read it aloud to your child

Since it's a quiet story, read it slowly and with lingering feeling. It's lovely to have deeper conversations with questions like, "Why did the fox ask to be tamed?" and "What is precious to you?" Suitable for ages 5-7, this classic is also one for parents to savor together.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. What age is The Little Prince good for?
A. It's suitable from ages 5-7, but it's a classic that resonates even more deeply when savored together with a parent.

Q. Won't the content be too difficult?
A. The picture book version for young children focuses on the core story and warm message, delivering it gently.

Q. What kind of conversation is good to have?
A. Try talking together about "seeing with the heart," "what is precious to me," and "the heart that nurtures a friend."
